edges.description: TPPII trims tripeptides from proteasome-generated oligopeptides, so its loss interrupts the recycling of protein-derived free amino acids.
TPP2 deficiency activates stress-induced death and senescence programmes in lymphocytes and fibroblasts; the molecular link from the lost peptidase step to senescence is not established.
TPPII destroys peptides overall, so its loss raises MHC class I on the cell surface.
edges.target: Increased MHC Class I Surface Expression

edges.description: Amino acid depletion triggers TFEB-dependent lysosomal biogenesis, which restores amino acid levels at the cost of an expanded lysosomal compartment.
The overabundant lysosomes take up and degrade the glycolytic enzyme hexokinase-2 by chaperone-mediated autophagy.
HK2 loss limits glycolytic flux; overexpressing HK2 restored glycolysis in TPPII-inhibited T cells.
Reduced glycolysis impairs IFN-gamma and IL-2 production in T cells and IL-1beta in monocytic cells; HK2 overexpression rescues both glycolysis and IFN-gamma.

Hypothesis only: the authors propose that defective aerobic glycolysis in neural cells underlies the neurodevelopmental delay, based on impaired glycolysis in a neuroblastoma line after TPPII inhibition.
The authors attribute the broad infection susceptibility to poor production of IFN-gamma, IL-2 and IL-1beta; the clinical link is inferred.
Same inferred link as for viral infections.
Senescence and death programmes in T-lineage cells are associated with lymphopenia in knockout mice; in patients the link is inferred.
T and B cell immunosenescence co-occur in patients; whether T cell senescence drives the B cell change is not shown.
Autoantibody-mediated red cell destruction is proposed to follow from B cell immunosenescence; the step is associative.
Same associative link as for autoimmune hemolytic anemia.
Reproduces stress-induced CD8 T cell senescence and the lymphopenia that follows, as seen in patient cells.
edges.limitations: Young knockout mice have normal thymic cellularity and the degenerative phenotype appears after one year, whereas patients present in infancy; the report does not describe Evans syndrome-like autoimmune cytopenias or a neurodevelopmental phenotype.

edges.limitations: Residual TPPII (<10%) remains, so this is a hypomorph rather than a null; CD8 T cell responses to viral epitopes were normal, which does not reproduce the patients' viral infection susceptibility.
